name: What a Data Privacy Agreement Must Say
title: What a Data Privacy Agreement Must Say
answer: A data privacy agreement is the contract that places an education company under a school's direct control. It matters because it sets the rules for how student data may be used, including whether the company can train general AI models on that data and when the data must be deleted. The agreement should be signed by a legal team or a designated administrator, not by an individual teacher.

crumbs.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule

sections.body: A data privacy agreement is the formal contract between a school or district and an education company, and it gives the school control over what happens to student data. The problem it solves is that without such an agreement, an outside company could decide how student information is used, retained, or shared. Many states and consortia publish model agreements, and districts can often adopt one that another district has already negotiated through the Student Data Privacy Consortium registry. That approach saves time and can give small districts protections similar to those of large districts. The agreement also identifies who signs on behalf of the school, which should be the legal team or a designated administrator rather than a teacher.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a district can begin with a model agreement from a state or consortium, or it can sign an agreement that another district has already negotiated through the Student Data Privacy Consortium registry. The text does not divide this practice by grade band, so the same contracting steps apply wherever an education company handles student data. The agreement should state that the company uses student data only to provide the service and not to train its general AI models. It should also require deletion of the data when the contract ends or when the school asks. Finally, it should list exactly which data fields the company collects, which is the part that raised concerns in Portland, as Figure 3.4 shows.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text does not give a research evidence label for this idea, so it rests on practice rather than research. The only specific reference it makes is to concerns in Portland about which data fields are collected, as shown in Figure 3.4. No study, number, or finding is provided beyond that reference. Readers should treat the agreement terms as practical guidance drawn from contracting practice, not as conclusions from a research trial.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets limits on who may sign and what the agreement must cover. A legal team or a designated administrator should sign, not an individual teacher, so the decision stays with the school rather than with a classroom employee. The company should use student data only to provide the service, should not use it to train general AI models, should delete it when the contract ends or when the school asks, and should list exactly which data fields it collects. The concern raised in Portland shows that unclear or broad data collection is a risk, and Figure 3.4 points to that concern. The text does not say that an agreement removes every risk, and it leaves the signing decision with the school's legal team or designated administrator.
